definitions.explanation: A decorated miniature shrine carried on poles by a group of people during festivals. It is believed to house the spirit of a deity during the procession.

examples.japanese: {祭|まつ}りで{神輿|みこし}が{通|とお}った。
examples.english: A portable shrine passed through during the festival.

examples.japanese: {町内会|ちょうないかい}のみんなで{神輿|みこし}を{担|かつ}いで{練|ね}り{歩|ある}いた。
examples.english: Everyone in the neighborhood association carried the portable shrine in a parade through the streets.

notes:
USAGE:
The core verb collocation is {神輿|みこし}を{担|かつ}ぐ (to carry a mikoshi on one's shoulders). The figurative idiom {神輿|みこし}を{担|かつ}ぐ can also mean to put someone forward as a figurehead or leader.

CULTURAL NOTE:
Portable shrines are central to many Japanese festivals ({祭|まつ}り). Carriers shout わっしょい as they parade the shrine through the streets. The shrine temporarily houses the local deity ({氏神|うじがみ}) during the festival.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {神輿|みこし}を{担|かつ}ぐ: to carry a portable shrine
- {神輿|みこし}を{練|ね}り{歩|ある}く: to parade the shrine through the streets
- {神輿|みこし}を{上|あ}げる: to lift up the shrine
